claims.text: Spark plasma sintering can reduce the sintering temperature required for ceramic powder compacts.
Rapid heating and ultra-short dwell times can preserve high densification at the reduced sintering temperature.
Rapid heating and ultra-short dwell times can provide controlled ceramic microstructures.
Mechanically alloyed alumina or zirconia compacts have a homogeneous distribution of fine particles.
Mechanically alloyed powders can be consolidated using spark plasma sintering.
Spark plasma sintering can be performed in a vacuum environment.
Rapid localized heating during SPS accelerates mass transport and densification.
Pulsed electrical current during SPS accelerates mass transport and densification.
The SPS heating regime limits grain growth.
High heating rates and short hold times reduce the time available for grain growth and phase changes.
Pulsed electrical current enhances diffusion kinetics and thereby aids densification at lower temperatures.
SPS-treated ceramics will attain comparable or improved densification at a lower temperature than conventionally sintered ceramics.
SPS-treated ceramics will attain comparable or improved mechanical properties at a lower temperature than conventionally sintered ceramics.
SPS treatment will reduce grain coarsening relative to conventional sintering.
Conventional sintering generally requires higher temperatures and longer dwell times than SPS.
Long conventional sintering treatments often cause excessive grain growth and greater energy consumption.
The temperature-reduction benefit of SPS applies primarily to electrically conductive or semiconductive ceramic powders.
Ceramics with very low electrical conductivity may not obtain the same SPS benefits.

contradictions.description: The experiment says that only the sintering method will differ, but it also deliberately assigns the SPS samples a lower temperature; therefore both method and temperature differ between groups.
